policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'I am a Jew' renders the pronoun alone; a connective μέν has no separate English exponent and the ASV gives none, so the wording does not distinguish the readings.
ἐμέ and με are the emphatic and enclitic forms of the same pronoun; ASV 'whom thou persecutest' renders either identically.
ASV reports only 'beheld indeed the light' with no clause answering καὶ ἔμφοβοι ἐγένοντο ('and became afraid'); the added clause is absent from the English.
ASV 'a devout man' is an ordinary rendering of either εὐλαβής or εὐσεβής; the English draws no distinction between reverent and pious here.
ἐμέ and με differ only as emphatic and enclitic forms; ASV 'came unto me' renders either. The verse's only note is an alternative_rendering about English wording and does not bear on the reading.
ASV 'calling on his name' renders the pronoun αὐτοῦ; the RP reading τοῦ κυρίου would give 'the name of the Lord', which the ASV does not have.
The variant is the presence of the Greek article before the noun; English 'testimony concerning me' supplies no exponent that would distinguish it.
ἐξεχύννετο and ἐξεχεῖτο are alternative imperfect forms of the same verb; ASV 'was shed' renders either.
ASV has 'and consenting, and keeping the garments' with no object of consent; the RP reading τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ would give 'consenting unto his death', which the English lacks.
κραυγαζόντων and κράζειν are near-synonymous verbs of shouting; ASV 'as they cried out' renders either.
τε and δέ are both connectives answered by ASV's initial 'And'; the English does not distinguish them.

The readings differ in word order and in εἰσάγεσθαι against ἄγεσθαι, but both are followed by εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, so ASV 'commanded him to be brought into the castle' renders either. The verse note is an alternative_rendering about 'chief captain' and does not bear on the reading.
εἴπας and εἰπών are alternative aorist participles of the same verb; ASV 'bidding' renders either.
ASV 'when they had tied him up with the thongs' has a plural subject, matching the plural προέτειναν rather than the singular προέτεινεν.
The readings differ only in the order of verb and dative object; ASV 'he went to the chief captain and told him' renders either order.
ASV reads 'What art thou about to do?' with nothing answering the imperative Ὅρα ('Take heed'/'See'), so the base reading without it is the one rendered.
Interrogative εἰ is regularly rendered as a direct question in English, so ASV 'Tell me, art thou a Roman?' does not exclude εἰ σύ and does not distinguish the readings.
δέ and τε are both connectives covered by ASV's 'And the chief captain answered'; the English does not distinguish them.
The readings differ only in the order of pronoun and verb; ASV 'when he knew that he was a Roman' renders either.
ὑπό and παρά with the genitive both mark the agent after a passive; ASV 'he was accused of the Jews' renders either.
ASV reads simply 'he loosed him' with nothing answering ἀπὸ τῶν δεσμῶν ('from his bands'), so the base reading without the phrase is the one rendered.
ASV 'commanded ... all the council to come together' renders the compound συνελθεῖn's 'together', which the simple ἐλθεῖν ('to come') would not supply.
πᾶν and ὅλον are both rendered 'all' before 'the council'; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV reads 'all the council', not 'their council'; the possessive αὐτῶν of the RP reading has no exponent in the English.
